issues.t: Key can slip out of Run and shut the van off (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly shuts off while driving, often after the key ring is bumped or the van hits a bump. Steering and braking get much heavier and the airbags may not work.
issues.why: The ignition switch could be knocked from Run into Accessory or Off. Volkswagen recalled 2009-2010 Routans several times to replace the ignition switch and key fobs.
issues.next: Run your VIN on Volkswagen's or NHTSA's recall lookup and have any open recall done for free. Until then, keep the key ring light and don't hang other keys from it.

issues.t: Power module (TIPM) failure: no-start, stalling or fuel pump that won't shut off
issues.sym: The van cranks but won't start, stalls while driving, or the fuel pump keeps running after the van is off and drains the battery. Some owners also see random warning lights or weak electrical systems.
issues.why: The Routan uses Chrysler's under-hood power module (TIPM). Its built-in fuel pump relay and circuits are known to fail on these minivans.
issues.next: Have a shop test fuel pump power and the TIPM before replacing the pump, battery or alternator. A repaired or replaced TIPM, or a fix for its fuel pump relay, is usually the cure.

issues.t: Harsh shifting, stuck in gear or transmission failure
issues.sym: Rough or delayed shifts, harsh downshifts when slowing down, the van stuck in one gear (limp mode), or a transmission that stops shifting altogether.
issues.why: The 6-speed automatic in these vans can wear internally, and its valve body, speed sensors, solenoids and control software are frequent trouble spots. Some cases were improved by a software update.
issues.next: Check the fluid and have the codes read at the first sign of trouble. Ask about software updates; a sensor or solenoid fix is much cheaper than a full replacement if caught early.

issues.t: Left cylinder head failure and misfires
issues.sym: Check engine light, a ticking noise from the engine, rough running or misfires, and loss of power.
issues.why: Early 3.6L V6 engines could overheat valve seats in the left cylinder head (cylinder 2). Chrysler extended coverage on the left head to 10 years or 150,000 miles for many 2011-2013 engines.
issues.next: Get the misfire codes read. If cylinder 2 keeps misfiring, ask a Volkswagen or Chrysler dealer whether your van's engine falls under the extended head coverage.

issues.t: Ticking from worn rocker arms
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping noise from the top of the engine, sometimes with a check engine light for a misfire.
issues.why: The roller rocker arms (cam followers) on the 3.6L V6 can wear or seize their rollers, which damages the camshaft if left alone.
issues.next: Have it checked soon; replacing rocker arms early avoids a much bigger camshaft repair. Many shops replace all of them at once.

issues.t: Oil filter housing and cooler leak
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front of the van, a burning oil smell, or oil and coolant mixing. The leak can come and go, which makes it hard to find.
issues.why: The 3.6L V6 has a plastic oil filter housing with a built-in oil cooler that cracks or leaks at its gaskets with age and heat.
issues.next: Have the top of the engine inspected for oil around the filter housing. The housing sits under the intake manifold, so most of the bill is labor.

issues.t: Heater hose Y-pipe and coolant hose leaks
issues.sym: Coolant smell, a sweet-smelling puddle, a low-coolant warning, overheating, or no heat from the vents.
issues.why: The plastic Y-shaped heater hose connectors and rubber coolant hoses on the 3.8L and 4.0L V6 crack and leak with age.
issues.next: Top up coolant only when the engine is cool and get the leak found quickly. Don't keep driving if the temperature gauge climbs.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes, the low oil light comes on, or blue smoke appears from the tailpipe.
issues.why: Some 3.8L and 4.0L engines burn oil, likely from worn piston rings or valve seals. Dealers often call moderate oil use normal.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up and keep it full. Document the usage; if it is heavy, a compression and leak-down test will show what is worn.

issues.t: Power sliding door hinge breaks or door sticks
issues.sym: A sliding door grinds, sticks, won't close on its own, reverses while closing, or rubs the body paint. Some doors hang loose from a broken hinge.
issues.why: The lower hinge and roller track wear and break, and the door module can be overly sensitive. Volkswagen issued fixes including hinge replacement and reprogramming.
issues.next: Have the hinge, track and door module checked. Lubricating the track helps, but a broken hinge should be replaced before it damages the door.

issues.t: Sliding door wiring can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: The power sliding door stops working, or you notice a burning smell near the door latch.
issues.why: On vans built June 2008 to July 2009, the door wiring harness could rub through at the lower hinge bracket and short, which could start a fire.
issues.next: Check for this open recall with your VIN; the dealer inspects and repairs the wiring for free.

issues.t: Brakes wear out early and rotors warp
issues.sym: Steering wheel shake or pedal pulsing when braking, squealing, and pads that need replacing much sooner than expected.
issues.why: The brakes on these heavy vans run hot and the rotors warp easily, which also wears pads quickly.
issues.next: Have pads and rotors measured. Quality rotors and pads, and not riding the brakes on hills, help them last longer.

issues.t: Sticking brake calipers
issues.sym: The van pulls to one side, one wheel gets very hot, a grinding noise from one corner, or brake pads that wear unevenly.
issues.why: Caliper pistons and slide pins corrode and stick, so a brake keeps dragging. Rear calipers and the parking brake cable are often involved.
issues.next: Have the brakes inspected soon; a dragging caliper ruins pads and rotors and can overheat the brakes.

issues.t: Network (CAN bus) faults cause many warning lights
issues.sym: Several warning lights come on at once, gauges act up, wipers or lights turn on by themselves, or the door locks stop working.
issues.why: Wiring or module faults on the van's data network (CAN bus) stop modules from talking to each other. Tracking the fault down can take a lot of time.
issues.next: Have a shop scan all modules, not just the engine. Check the battery and grounds first, since low voltage can trigger network faults.

issues.t: A/C blows warm from leaks or compressor failure
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, especially from the rear vents, or works only now and then.
issues.why: Refrigerant leaks at the rear A/C lines and rear evaporator are common on these vans, and compressors fail too.
issues.next: Have the system leak-tested with dye before recharging. Recharging without fixing the leak just wastes money.

issues.t: Alternator failure and battery light
issues.sym: The battery light comes on, the lights dim, and the van may die while driving or not restart.
issues.why: Alternators on the 3.6L V6 Routan fail with some regularity. A loose or worn serpentine belt or tensioner can also stop the battery from charging.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested right away. Check the belt and tensioner too when replacing the alternator.

issues.t: Worn wheel bearings
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed and may change when turning.
issues.why: Front and rear wheel bearings wear out on these heavy vans. A Chrysler bulletin covered front bearings on some vans.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked. A badly worn bearing can overheat and become unsafe, so don't put it off.

issues.t: Tire pressure sensors fail or light flickers
issues.sym: The tire pressure light comes on or flickers even when tires are fine, or a sensor stops reading.
issues.why: The tire pressure sensors corrode at the valve stems and their batteries wear out with age.
issues.next: Check the tires with a gauge first. Failed sensors can be replaced one at a time and need to be relearned.

issues.t: Rear axle may crack (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning before a failure; you might notice clunks or odd handling from the rear.
issues.why: A small number of 2009 Routans had a rear axle that could fracture, which raises the risk of a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Airbag control unit can corrode (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on.
issues.why: Corrosion in the airbag control unit's power supply could stop airbags from deploying in a crash or set one off without a crash.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; the dealer repairs it for free.

issues.t: Rear wheel hub may be faulty (recall)
issues.sym: Possible noise or looseness at a rear wheel; there may be no warning.
issues.why: A handful of 2012 Routans got rear hub and bearing assemblies that may not last, which could lead to a wheel coming off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Rough idle after a cold start
issues.sym: The engine idles roughly or shakes for a short time after starting cold.
issues.why: Engine computer programming on early vans; Volkswagen released a software update for it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the engine computer update has been done.

issues.t: Power steering leaks and pump noise
issues.sym: Whining from the engine bay when turning, heavier steering, or power steering fluid leaking.
issues.why: The power steering pump bearing and return hoses on these vans can wear and leak.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for leaks. A noisy pump that keeps losing fluid should be fixed before it fails.

issues.t: Moan or hum on cold starts
issues.sym: A moan, whistle or loud hum right after starting on cold mornings that fades as the van warms up.
issues.why: Owners trace this to the power steering and engine accessories on the 3.6L vans; a Chrysler service bulletin addressed it on some vans.
issues.next: Mention it to the dealer and ask about the related bulletin. It's mostly an annoyance, but have fluid levels checked.

issues.t: Sunroof and liftgate water leaks
issues.sym: Water inside the cabin, wet headliner or damp cargo area after rain.
issues.why: Sunroof seals and the liftgate's upper seal can leak, and clogged drains make it worse.
issues.next: Clear the sunroof drains and check the seals. A body shop can reseal the liftgate gasket.

issues.t: Radio and Bluetooth freezing or distortion
issues.sym: The radio freezes, rejects Bluetooth, or distorts sound when playing from an iPod.
issues.why: Software faults in the factory radio; an update fixed many units.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for any radio software update before replacing the unit.
